3. Shri Sharma has submitted that earlier, this Court taking note of the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties dismissed the said petition vide order dated 28.11.2023 as the Court,
at that stage, was not inclined to conduct a mini trial.

He has further submitted that the subsequent petition which is the present one filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is not maintainable for the reason that whatever submissions are being raised here in this petition and material placed by the petitioner so as to initiate proceedings for quashing the FIR and also the charge-sheet, have already been taken note of by the Court and, therefore, there is no drastic change to give a fresh cause of action to the petitioner to challenge the proceedings and to file a petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C.

He has submitted that the Supreme Court in the case of Bhisham Lal Verma Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and another reported in 2023 LiveLaw (SC) 935 has observed as to under what circumstances, subsequent petition can be filed by the accused.

He has submitted that in such a circumstance when all the material have already been taken note of by the Court on earlier occasion,
in the light of the law laid down in the case of case of Bhisham Lal Verma (supra), this petition deserves to be dismissed as not maintainable.

4. In rebuttal, Shri Datt, learned Senior Counsel also relying upon the case of Bhishm Lal Verma (supra) has submitted that the circumstances as considered by the Supreme Court, permit the petitioner to file the instant petition.

His main leg of argument is that on earlier occasion only FIR was available with the petitioner and that had been challenged by him but at this stage charge-sheet has been filed that too on 09.03.2024 and material placed by the prosecution in support of the contentions made in the FIR and, therefore, challenging the FIR and M.Cr.C-15120-2024 charge-sheet are altogether different aspect and scope of entertaining the petition in regard to quashing the FIR and of charge-sheet are altogether different.

He has submitted that the law laid down by the Supreme Court very clearly permits the petitioner to file a subsequent petition because this petition has been filed seeking quashing of charge-sheet and as such, there is nothing wrong committed by him.

He has also submitted that in view of the allegations attributed in the FIR and the material placed by the respondents by way of charge-sheet are not sufficient to constitute an offence of Section 376 of IPC.

He has submitted that it is the consensual relationship between the parties and allegation with regard to developing physical relation on a false promise of marriage is absolutely wrong because prosecutrix was fully aware of the fact that petitioner is a married person and that allegation is nothing but a false allegation just to constitute an offence of Section 376 of IPC.

Shri Datt has furhter placed reliance upon the decisions passed in the case of Rakesh Walia Vs.

In view of the objection raised by learned counsel for the respondents and submissions made by counsel for the parties, this Court has to determine whether the subsequent petition by the same party under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. is maintainable or not.
Both the parties have relied upon the Bhisham Lal Verma (supra).
The relevant part of the order of the said case as under:-

"10. In S. Madan Kumar vs. K. Arjunan , the Madras High Court observed that a person who invokes Section 482 Cr.P.C. should honestly come before the Court raising all the pleas available to him at that point of time and he is not supposed to approach the Court with instalment pleas.

entities.text: S. Madan Kumar vs. K. Arjunan
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It was further observed that there may be a change of circumstances during the course of criminal proceedings which would give scope for the person aggrieved to invoke the inherent jurisdiction of the Court, but when he is posted with all the facts and M.Cr.C-15120-2024 circumstances of a case

,
he cannot withhold part of it for the purpose of filing yet another petition seeking the same relief.
11. We are in complete agreement with these observations of the Madras High Court.

Though it is clear that there can be no blanket rule that a second petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C. would not lie in any situation and it would depend upon the facts and circumstances of the individual case, it is not open to a person aggrieved to raise one plea after the other, by invoking the jurisdiction of the High Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C., though all such pleas were very much available even at the first instance.

Permitting the filing of successive petitions under Section 482 Cr.P.C. ignoring this principle would enable an ingenious accused to effectively stall the proceedings against him to suit his own interest and convenience, by filing one petition after another under Section 482 Cr.P.C., irrespective of when the cause therefor arose.
Such abuse of process cannot be permitted.

12. In the case on hand, the filing of the charge sheet and the cognizance thereof by the Court concerned were well before the filing of the first petition under Section 482 Cr.P.C., wherein challenge was made only to the sanction order.
That being so, the petitioner was not at liberty to again invoke the inherent jurisdiction of the High Court in relation to the charge sheet and the cognizance order at a later point of time.

The 5 (1990) 2 SCC 437 6 (1981) 1 SCC 500 7 (2002) 10 SCC 401 8 (2006) 1 MWN (Cri) DCC 1 = 2006 SCC Online Mad 94 4 impugned order passed by the Allahabad High Court holding to this effect is, therefore, incontrovertible on all counts and does not warrant interference."

A plain reading of aforesaid makes it amply clear that there is no complete bar for filing a successive petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C., however, change in the circumstances should be there so also in the facts, which could not be considered by the Court at the time of entertaining earlier petition.

6. However, in the present case, undisputably, when the first petition was filed i.e. W.P.
No.10662/2023 under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the only challenge was with regard to the FIR but on the said date, since no charge- sheet was filed, therefore, this Court declined to Bhagwat Prasad Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184539588/

However, this petition has been filed challenging the charge-sheet filed by the prosecution on 09.03.2024 whereas earlier petition i.e.
W.P. No.10662/2023 got decided by the Court by order dated 28.11.2023 meaning thereby, that petition was filed challenging the FIR only that too in a very M.Cr.C-15120-2024 preliminary stage but the present petition has been filed after filing of the charge- sheet.
7.

Although, as per Shri Manoj Sharma, learned Senior counsel for the respondent No.2, the grounds raised by the petitioner in the said petition and material pointed out were same as are being pointed in the present petition but I am not convinced with the submission made by Shri Sharma because scope of interfering in the FIR and scope of interfering in the charge-sheet are different for the reason that at the time of considering the petition challenging the FIR, the Court was confined to consider the contents of the FIR but while challenging the charge-sheet, the Court can also consider and examine the material placed by the prosecution along with the charge-sheet and as such, second petition challenging the charge-sheet on the basis of material available, is maintainable in light of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in case of Bhisham Lal Verma (supra).

Thus, the objection raised by learned Senior counsel for the respondent No.2, in my opinion, is not sustainable and,
therefore, the same is rejected holding that this petition can be entertained by the High Court though it is a subsequent petition by the same party seeking quashing of FIR and also the charge-sheet filed by the prosecution.

8. Now, in pursuance of the material available on record that has been filed by the prosecution along with the charge-sheet, it is clear that in the 164 statement of the prosecutrix, she has admitted this fact that she came in contact with the present petitioner on 31.07.2020 when he called her at Sidhi where he was posted and then they talked to each other for two hours and thereafter the prosecutrix went back to Banaras.

Then again petitioner called the prosecutrix and she came to Sidhi and stayed at Hotel Basant Palace and on the same day at around 10.30 p.m., the petitioner took her to a deserted place and developed physical relationship without her consent and thereafter he dropped her to the hotel.
According to her, M.Cr.C-15120-2024 on 17.12.2020, the petitioner applied vermilion (sindoor) and also tied mangalsutra on her neck and thereafter dropped her back at Hotel Madhusudan.
According to her, the petitioner asked her to go to Mumbai for some time so that he would convince his family members in the meantime.
She has further deposed that when petitioner's phone was continuously switched off, she came to Sidhi in Feburary, 2021 and kept trying to contact him but she could not meet him.

However as per prosecution case, after sometime,
the petitioner made her stay in a rented room and used to take her out and have sexual intercourse with her.
From 06th December to 14th December, the petitioner sexually exploited her and when she asked him to take her to his house, he started beating her.
According to the 164 statement, the petitioner also tried to kill the prosecutrix.
Even after this, the petitioner continued to commit rape with her forcefully.
According to her, the last time, the petitioner went to a deserted place was on 12.02.2023 and again forcefully abused and raped her.

The petitioner did not tell her that he was already married and had two children and stated that now since she knew everything about him,
therefore, he will not marry her and he sent her back to Mumbai.

sentences.text: There were several material placed by the prosecution with the charge- sheet so as to show that the statement given by the prosecutrix does not tally with the factual aspect as has been described by her.
It is also relevant from perusal of the record that both the parties have made complaint against each other.
The petitioner was a married person and that information was available in the electronic media and the prosecutrix was also aware of the said fact.

There were certain photographs available on record showing the prosecutrix with the children of the petitioner which clearly indicate that even after knowing the fact that petitioner was married, the prosecutrix continued to remain in relationship with him.
10. The offence got registered against the petitioner under Sections 376(2) M.Cr.C-15120-2024 (n) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code.

According to counsel for the petitioner, in pursuance of a complaint made by the prosecutrix, earlier also on 16.03.2019, an offence vide FIR No. 50/2019 at Police Station Kotwali, District Varanasi (U.P.) under Sections 147, 323, 447, 452, 427, 504, 506 and 354(Kha) got registered against the petitioner.

However, on 14.10.2020, the prosecutrix appeared before the Court of ACJM at Varanasi and filed an affidavit and taking a somersault had stated that no such incident as alleged in the complaint took place and as such, that affidavit resulted into acquittal of all the 15 accused persons named by her in the FIR.
Relevant documents have also been filed along with I.A. No.11659/2024 and the same is available on record.

There is another document filed showing a written complaint of the prosecutrix made against one Sandeep Tiwari dated 10.02.2020 before S.P. Bhadohi, U.P. alleging commission of rape on the false pretext of marriage.
Subsequently, she arrayed his uncle who was a sitting MLA and his 05 sons and as such, offence got registered vide Crime No.40/2020 against all the seven persons.
Copy of the FIR is also available on record.

Thereafter, the prosecutrix appeared before the Sessions Court at Bhadohi in Sessions Trial No.130/2022 wherein her statement has been recorded and in her statement, she took a somersault and stated that no such incident took place.

It is relevant to note that earlier Sandeep Tiwari and his wife have also lodged an FIR against the prosecutrix and offence under Sections 507, 500, 504 and 506 of the Indian Penal Code got registered against her.

There were certain other documents indicating that it is the prosecutrix, who was persuading the petitioner to develop physical relationship but he refused to do so saying that he is already married and it is not possible for him to marry her.

11. Even otherwise, in view of the facts mentioned in the FIR and also in view of the 164 statement of the prosecutrix, it is clear that prosecutrix continued to be in physical relationship with the petitioner for almost three years and then M.Cr.C-15120-2024 lodged the FIR.
12 . The Supreme Court in the case of Mahesh Damu Khare Vs. State of Maharashtra and others reported in 2024 SCC Online 3471

the case of 376 IPC on a false promise of marriage

but taking note of the fact and observation made by the Supreme Court it is clear that if relationship is continued for long then it cannot be presumed that the said relationship is developed due to false promise of marriage.

The observation made by the Supreme Court is as under :-
"22.

In our view, if a man is accused of having sexual relationship by making a false promise of marriage and if he is to be held criminally liable, any such physical Bhagwat Prasad Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184539588/
5 relationship must be traceable directly to the false promise made and not qualified by other circumstances or consideration.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: A woman may have reasons to have physical relationship other than the promise of marriage made by the man, such as personal liking for the male partner without insisting upon formal marital ties.

Thus, in a situation where physical relationship is maintained for a prolonged period knowingly by the woman, it cannot be said with certainty that the said physical relationship was purely because of the alleged promise made by the appellant to marry her.

Thus,
unless it can be shown that the physical relationship was purely because of the promise of marriage, thereby having a direct nexus with the physical relationship without being influenced by any other consideration, it cannot be said that there was vitiation of consent under misconception of fact.
Thus, from the above it appears that it is more of an extra-marital affair during the aforesaid period without any insistence by the complainant for getting married to the appellant.

The fact that the complainant continued to have a physical relationship for a long time without any insistence on marriage would indicate the unlikelihood of any such promise made by the appellant for marrying her and it rather indicates that the relationship was a consensual one.

In our opinion, the longer the duration of the physical relationship between the partners without protest and insistence by the female partner for marriage would be indicative of a consensual relationship rather than a relationship based on false promise of marriage by the male partner and thus,
based on misconception of fact".

(Emphasis supplied)
13. Further, the Supreme Court in the case of Bishwajyoti Chatterjee Vs. State of West Bengal and another reported in 2025 Live Law (SC) 404, the Supreme Court again considered the aspect as to what type of relationship can be M.Cr.C-15120-2024 considered to be of consensual relationship and what type of evidence is required to prove that such relationship is consensual.

entities.text: Bishwajyoti Chatterjee Vs. State of West Bengal and another reported in 2025 Live Law (SC) 404
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The observation made by the Supreme Court relying upon another Supreme Court judgment passed in Uday vs State of Karnataka reported in (2003) 4 SCC 46 observed in para 17 as under :-
"In the ultimate analysis, the tests laid down by the courts provide at best guidance to the judicial mind while considering a question of consent, but the court must, in each case, consider the evidence before it and the surrounding circumstances, before reaching a conclusion, because each case has its own peculiar facts which may have a bearing on the question whether the consent was voluntary, or was given under a misconception of fact".
14.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Further, it is observed by the Supreme Court in the said case as to when relationship cannot be considered to be of a false promise of marriage.

The observation of the Supreme Court is as under :-
Bhagwat Prasad Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184539588/
6 "20.

entities.text: Bhagwat Prasad Pandey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We find that there is a growing tendency of resorting to initiation of criminal proceedings when relationships turn sour.

Every consensual relationship, where a possibility of marriage may exist, cannot be given a colour of a false pretext to marry,
in the event of a fall out.
It is such lis that amounts to an abuse of process of law, and it is under such circumstances, that we deem fit to terminate the proceedings at the stage of charge itself".
(Emphasis supplied)

15. Thus, it is clear from the aforesaid enunciation of law and observations made by the Supreme Court so as to substantiate the relationship between the parties cannot be considered to be a relationship developed on a false pretext of marriage.

16. In the present case also, if the existing factual circumstances as narrated by the prosecutrix in the FIR are considered to be true at their face value, then it is clear that the said relationship is not on a false promise of marriage and as such material ingredients of Section 69 of BNS are completely missing and this relationship cannot be considered to be a relationship developed on a false promise of marriage and merely such allegation cannot be made basis for initiating proceeding because there can be certain reasons showing bitterness in the M.Cr.C-15120-2024 relationship between the parties and as such, without there being any cogent evidence, proceeding under Section 69 of BNS cannot be initiated.

I am not convinced with a submissions made by counsel for the respondents,
but, on the other hand, looking to the facts and circumstances of the present case and the view taken by the Supreme Court, as has been quoted hereinabove, in my opinion it is a malicious prosecution as no material ingredient of Section 69 BNS is available and as such FIR, in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajanlal reported in 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335, can be quashed.

entities.text: State of Haryana and others Vs. Ch. Bhajanlal reported in 1992 Supp. (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
17. Thus, in the facts and circumstances of the case, I am not convinced with the submission made by counsel for the respondents justifying registration of case and its prosecution as the facts and circumstances existing in this case and discussed hereinabove clearly indicate that this prosecution cannot go on as it is malicious and even otherwise, offence of Section 376 of IPC is not made out because it cannot be considered to be a rape as defined under Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code.
18.
Ex consequentia, this petition is allowed.

The FIR registered against the petitioner vide FIR/Crime No.378/2023 at Police Station Sidhi Kotwali, District Sidhi, for the offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 506 of the Indian Penal Code is not sustainable and as such, it is hereby quashed.

It is further made clear that all further proceedings i.e. the charge-sheet based upon the said FIR against the present petitioner shall also stand quashed.
19.
With the aforesaid, the petition stands allowed.
No costs.
(SANJAY DWIVEDI) JUDGE rao
